Offshore Energy Services.heading: Offshore Energy Services
Offshore Energy Services.text: Many energy industry observers believe that the combination of increasing long-term energy demand tied to global economic growth, geopolitical conflicts leading to energy security concerns, and a growing desire for more efficient and consistent energy sources are contributing to the shift towards deepwater and ultra-deepwater drilling. While initial costs are higher, deepwater and ultra-deepwater regions often hold vast, untapped reservoirs of oil and natural gas that can produce energy over decades while proving better returns on invested capital over their useful lives compared to onshore wells. In recent years, innovations in deepwater technology, such as advanced seismic imaging and high-pressure drilling equipment, have reduced exploratory risks and improved operational efficiency and safety, making previously inaccessible reserves viable for development. As energy exploration, development and production moves further offshore and into deeper waters, more heavy and medium helicopters and newer technology helicopters are expected to be required by our customers. In addition, markets such as Nigeria and Brazil continue to show growth and increased demand for vertical lift. We believe we are well positioned to benefit from higher pricing and improved cash flows as legacy contracts expire and are renegotiated at higher rates and on better terms for the service provider.

Offshore Energy Services.heading: Offshore Energy Services
Offshore Energy Services.text: Many energy industry observers believe that the combination of increasing long-term energy demand tied to global economic growth, geopolitical conflicts leading to energy security concerns, and a growing desire for more efficient and consistent energy sources are contributing to the shift towards deepwater and ultra-deepwater drilling. While initial costs are higher, deepwater and ultra-deepwater regions often hold vast, untapped reservoirs of oil and natural gas that can produce energy over decades while proving better returns on invested capital over their useful lives compared to onshore wells. In recent years, innovations in deepwater technology, such as advanced seismic imaging and high-pressure drilling equipment, have reduced exploratory risks and improved operational efficiency and safety, making previously inaccessible reserves viable for development. As energy exploration, development and production moves further offshore and into deeper waters, more heavy and medium helicopters and newer technology helicopters are expected to be required by our customers. In addition, markets such as Nigeria and Brazil continue to show growth and increased demand for vertical lift. We believe we are well positioned to benefit from higher pricing and improved cash flows as legacy contracts expire and are renegotiated at higher rates and on better terms for the service provider.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 66%, 26% and 8% of our total revenues were derived from Offshore Energy Services, Government Services and Other Services, respectively.
During the year ended December 31, 2024, approximately 68%, 23% and 9% of our total revenues were derived from Offshore Energy Services, Government Services and Other Services, respectively.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, our top ten customers accounted for approximately 63% of revenues, and the combined revenues from our three largest customers accounted for 36% of our revenues.
For example, there has recently been political and social unrest in Nigeria, where we derived 13% and 12% of our revenues during the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

We generated approximately 66% of our consolidated revenues from Offshore Energy Services during the year ended December 31, 2025, and the majority of our customers are engaged in offshore energy production, exploration and development.

Our UK SAR contract, which accounted for approximately 19% of our revenues for year ended December 31, 2025, allows the DfT to cancel the UK SAR contract for any reason upon notice and payment of a specified cancellation fee based on the number of bases reduced as a result of the exercise and the timing of the exercise.
Our Government Services contracts accounted for approximately 26% of our revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.

During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, approximately 66% and 68%, respectively, of our total revenues were derived from Offshore Energy Services while approximately 26% and 23%, respectively, were derived from Government Services and approximately 8% and 9%, respectively, were derived from Other Services.
Our success depends on our ability to attract and retain qualified personnel, including pilots and engineers.
Our success depends on our ability to attract and retain skilled personnel, specifically our pilots and engineers.

Additionally, expansion of our business depends on our ability to operate in additional international markets, which may be adversely affected by numerous factors, including but not limited to: (i) local regulations restricting foreign ownership of helicopter operators;
The number of aircraft sales and the amount of gains and losses recorded on these sales depends on a wide variety of factors and is inherently unpredictable.
The timely and adequate supply of fuel to meet operational demand depends on the continued availability of reliable fuel supply sources as well as related service and delivery infrastructure.

We rely on our information technology infrastructure and management information systems to operate and record almost every aspect of our business, including confidential or personal information belonging to us, our employees, customers, and suppliers.

Because our business depends on the level of activity in the offshore energy industry, existing or future laws, regulations, treaties or international agreements related to greenhouse gases and climate change, including incentives to conserve energy or use alternative energy sources, could have a negative impact on our business if such laws, regulations, treaties or agreements reduce worldwide demand for offshore energy or limit drilling opportunities.

Share repurchases and dividends are authorized and determined by the Board in its sole discretion and depend upon a number of factors, including the Company’s results of operations, financial condition, cash requirements, growth opportunities, restrictions in our financing arrangements and other factors that the Board may deem relevant.

The timing and amount of dividends will depend on the Company’s results of operations, financial condition, cash requirements, growth opportunities, restrictions in our financing arrangements and other factors that the Board may deem relevant.

Our primary sources of liquidity include unrestricted cash balances, cash flows from operations, borrowings under our ABL Facility and, from time to time, we may obtain additional liquidity through the issuance of equity, debt, other financing options or through asset sales.

The declaration and payment of dividends will be subject at all times to the discretion of the Board, and the timing and amount of dividends will depend on the Company’s results of operations, financial condition, cash requirements, growth opportunities, restrictions in our financing arrangements and other factors that the Board may deem relevant.
